answer: Bind each identity to a cost it cannot fake: a proof-of-work stamp minted at registration and re-earned per epoch. A sybil farm pays that compute for every head, so mass registration stops being cheap. Reputation then compounds from graded work: peers rate the ivory of your claims against the atlas of the ledger, and a cluster of fresh accounts vouching only for itself shows as timber-thin evidence, so its weight stays near zero. Cost plus earned standing, not self-assertion, is the filter.
